column2: State what students are expected to learn, know, understand, or be able to do by the end of the lesson. This should align with curriculum outcomes and clearly communicate the focus of the learning experience.

Describe how students (and teachers) will know if the learning intention has been achieved. Include specific, observable, and measurable indicators of success—ideally written as student-friendly “I can” statements.

Detail the explicit teaching or direct instruction that introduces new content or skills. This includes teacher-led explanations, modeling, demonstrations, or worked examples that build a foundation for student understanding.

Describe how the teacher will work alongside students to support and scaffold learning. This may involve questioning, prompts, small group instruction, or targeted feedback as students begin to practice new skills or apply new knowledge.

Explain how students will work together to explore and apply their learning. This could include partner work, group tasks, peer discussions, or cooperative problem-solving activities that promote communication and shared understanding.

Outline the tasks students will complete individually to demonstrate their learning. These activities should allow students to apply what they’ve learned, build independence, and provide opportunities for formative or summative assessment.

Describe how students will reflect on their learning at the end of the lesson. This could include self-assessment, journaling, discussion, or sharing insights. Reflection should help consolidate learning and connect to the success criteria.

Explain how instruction, content, or tasks will be adjusted to support the diverse needs of students. Include strategies for varying complexity, providing scaffolds or extensions, offering choices, or responding to specific learning profiles.

List all materials, tools, and supports needed to deliver the lesson effectively. This includes physical items (e.g., handouts, manipulatives), digital tools (e.g., videos, apps), and any prep or environmental setup required.
